title.en: World War II: causes and outbreak

text.en: In the early 1920s a worker in Germany could be paid in the morning with a wheelbarrow full of notes, and by evening the notes bought less bread. People carried money in wheelbarrows. That anger, and the leaders who fed on it, is where World War II begins.

World War I was fought from 1914 to 1918 and World War II from 1939 to 1945, and both are called world wars because the fighting covered huge areas and killed very many civilians as well as soldiers.
In both wars Britain, France, Russia and the United States fought against an alliance led by Germany, and in the second war Germany's allies were Italy and Japan.
The Treaty of Versailles, signed in June 1919, angered Germans with three clauses: they gave up land to the west, north and east, they had to disarm to a very small force, and they had to pay for the cost of the war.
The immediate and main cause of the war was the aggressive military drive of a resurgent Germany and a fast-growing Japan.
The problems of the post-war years led to extreme right-wing dictatorships in Italy under Mussolini, in Germany under Hitler and in Spain under Franco.
Germany suffered high unemployment and terrible inflation, its currency became almost worthless, and people blamed the reparations, although the demands were later reduced after several rounds of talks.
Adolf Hitler used this anger: a gifted speaker, he founded the National Socialist party, the Nazis, and built support on the idea that Germans were a pure Aryan race and on deep hatred of Jews.
Hitler came to power in 1933 and ruled until 1945.
Against the Treaty, Hitler began to rearm Germany, and the arms factories and army recruitment, paid by heavy government spending, revived the economy and removed unemployment.
The League of Nations was set up by the Treaty on the initiative of President Woodrow Wilson to mediate between countries and act against aggression, but the United States stayed out and the other Allies avoided intervening, so the League stayed ineffective.
Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935 and Albania in 1939, and when Emperor Haile Selassie appealed to the League he got no help.
Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931 and China in 1937, seizing Beijing, and the Allies and the League did nothing.
After Mussolini's invasion of Ethiopia broke Italy's ties with Britain and France, Italy drew closer to Germany, and the Rome-Berlin Axis appeared in 1936, later widening into the Rome-Berlin-Tokyo Axis when Japan joined.
In 1938 Hitler took Austria and Czechoslovakia, claiming that the German-speaking people of the Sudetenland should join one nation.
Britain and France stayed non-interventionist under Prime Ministers Baldwin and Chamberlain, and the United States, busy recovering from the Great Depression, was indifferent to the outside world.
In 1938 Chamberlain signed the Munich Pact, a shameful acceptance of the German takeover of the Sudetenland, and in 1939 the Soviet Union signed its own non-aggression pact with Germany, since the Western powers and the Soviets distrusted each other.
Hitler broke his Munich promise at once, invaded Czechoslovakia in 1939 and then attacked Poland, and Britain and France declared war on Germany in September 1939.
Italy joined Germany in June 1940 and Japan joined in September 1940, completing the Axis powers.

problem.en: Which three clauses of the Treaty of Versailles angered Germany, and how did the anger help Hitler?

text.en: Germany lost land in the west, north and east, had to disarm, and had to pay reparations for the war.

why.en: These were the three clauses the Germans resented most.

text.en: Inflation and unemployment made the reparations feel unbearable, so people turned to a leader who promised a glorious past.

why.en: Hitler used oratory and the idea of racial superiority to win support.

text.en: Hitler came to power in 1933 and began to rearm in breach of the Treaty.

why.en: The rearmament revived the economy, which made him popular.

prompt.en: Explain why the League of Nations failed to stop the aggression of the 1930s.

requiredIdeas.en: The United States did not join it
It could not act against Italy over Ethiopia or Japan over Manchuria

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the League had its own army
Thinking the League stopped Germany in 1936

points.en: Hitler in power in 1933; dictators in Italy, Germany, Spain.
League of Nations failed: no US, no action on Ethiopia and Manchuria.
Axis 1936; Munich Pact 1938; war declared September 1939.
